chunks: And it is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Qasim, the freedman of Abi Ayyub, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the sun sets, the time for the two prayers has entered until the middle of the night, except that this [prayer] is before this [prayer]. And when the sun declines (moves from its zenith), the time for the two prayers has entered, except that this [prayer] is before this [prayer]."
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times for Dhuhr and Asr prayers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the temporal boundaries for Dhuhr and Asr, establishing that their combined window extends from the sun's decline (or sunset, depending on the specific interpretation of 'gharabat' vs 'zalat' in this chain) until the middle of the night. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of combining prayers within their respective times, distinguishing the precedence of Dhuhr over Asr while emphasizing the flexibility of the 'middle of the night' deadline for both.
